name: David Kakabadze
medium: Watercolour and gouache on paper, forms held by soft, thick, blurred dark outlines, colour bleeding inside them
colour: light paper with soft washes of rose, ochre, violet, cobalt and teal, thick blurred dark-blue outlines
form: Breton houses, windmills, castles, harbours and sailing boats on rippled water, stylised waves as repeated curls
never: never photographic, never oil-paint texture, never a dark overall ground, never printed text or letters
consent: PUBLIC DOMAIN — the artist died in 1952 (more than 70 years ago); the works are reproductions of his paintings. Portrait: his own self-portrait (public domain).
bio: David Kakabadze (1889–1952), the Georgian avant-garde painter, spent most of the 1920s in Paris and painted the coast of Brittany again and again — houses, mills, harbours and boats in watercolour, held by soft, glowing dark outlines. This is the light, lyrical side of one of the founders of Georgian modern art.
charterBy: Claude's draft from the 8 Breton watercolours (public domain), 2026-09-29 — the oils and the abstractions retired at the owner's word
bioGe: დავით კაკაბაძე (1889–1952), ქართული ავანგარდის მხატვარი, 1920-იან წლებში პარიზში ცხოვრობდა და ბრეტანის სანაპიროს არაერთხელ ხატავდა — სახლებს, წისქვილებს, ნავსადგურებსა და ნავებს აკვარელით, რბილი, მოკაშკაშე მუქი კონტურებით. ეს ქართული თანამედროვე ხელოვნების ერთ-ერთი ფუძემდებლის მსუბუქი, ლირიკული მხარეა.
